title: Nike bets everything on a rookie: signing Michael Jordan
decisionMaker: Phil Knight and Rob Strasser (Nike), with Sonny Vaccaro pushing the idea
decision: In 1984 a struggling Nike (first quarterly loss, behind Reebok and Converse) offered Michael Jordan, a rookie who had not played an NBA game and who preferred Adidas, about $500,000 a year for five years in cash (about $2.5 million, roughly three times any other shoe deal), plus royalties and his own shoe line, Air Jordan, instead of spreading its basketball marketing over several players. The 'whole budget on one player' framing is Sonny Vaccaro's account and the credit for the deal is disputed.
hook: Five hundred thousand dollars a year, for a rookie who had not played a single NBA game. Three times the record for a shoe deal. Today that bet is a brand that sells more than five billion dollars of shoes a year.
